source_statement: Finite-support reconstruction; confirms SECTIONS A.32. \label{prop:ghost-finite-support} Every pair in \(\mathcal G_{\rm ord}\) for which the valuation vector of at least one of \(A\), \(B\), or \(A/B\) is finitely supported has the form \[ (A,B)=(\kappa(t),\kappa(1-t)), \qquad t\in\mathbb Q\setminus\{0,1\}, \] for a unique \(t\), and \(t_p=t\) at every finite prime.
source_depends_on: Actual local ordinary equalities; prime valuations and completed Kummer maps
audit_scope: The complete finite-support reconstruction is re-proved, including finite support of A/B and equality of every finite ordinary local point.

source_statement: Infinite ramification at every coefficient prime. \label{prop:ghost-infinite-ramification} For an ordinary pair with infinite support, its abelian \(\ell\)-primary Kummer component ramifies at infinitely many rational primes, for every \(\ell\). Its abelian component at no \(\ell\) is the component of a rational point or a cuspidal section. For every finite set of rational primes \(S\), the vectors \((v_q(A),v_q(B))\), \(q\notin S\), span \(\mathbb Q_\ell^2\) for every \(\ell\). In particular the abelian geometric inertia images outside any finite set containing \(\ell\) generate an open submodule of \(\mathbb Z_\ell(1)^2\).
source_depends_on: C.1.1; ordinary local valuation patterns
audit_scope: Infinite ramification at every coefficient prime is proved. The stronger span and cusp clauses follow because ordinary valuation vectors lie on (m,0),(0,m),(m,m): rank at most one outside a finite set makes A, B or A/B finitely supported, contrary to E.101. Two independent vectors generate an open Z_ell-submodule.

source_statement: Compact higher-weight cocycles. \label{lem:ghost-higher-z1} For every \(r\geq2\), the module \(Z^1_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,\mathbb Z_\ell(r))\) is a finite free \(\mathbb Z_\ell\)-module, and its module topology is its compact-open topology. Every such cocycle factors through \(G_{\mathbb Q,\{\ell,\infty\}}\).
source_depends_on: Tame inertia weights; finite ramification outside ell; finite-coefficient global cohomology
audit_scope: Higher-weight literal continuous cocycles are finite free and compact; the fixed-ramification factorization is retained.

source_statement: The integral Hall coordinate model. \label{lem:ghost-hall-model} For fixed \(r\), ordered basic commutators of weights at most \(r\) identify \(N_{r,\ell}\), as a topological space, with \(\mathbb Z_\ell^{h_r}\). Multiplication, inversion, and taking \(\mathbb Z_\ell\)-powers have coordinates given by rational polynomials. Their denominators have a fixed bound depending on \(r\). The quotient to \(N_{r-1,\ell}\) deletes the weight-\(r\) coordinates, and setting those coordinates equal to zero gives a continuous section of this quotient as a map of spaces. The coordinate functions of \(g(u)\), for the actual action of \(G\), are rational polynomials in the coordinates of \(u\), with coefficients that are continuous functions of \(g\). They too have bounded denominators at each fixed \(r\).
source_depends_on: Integral Hall collection and actual free nilpotent pro-ell quotients
audit_scope: Integral Hall coordinate model, bounded rational denominators and the actual continuous arithmetic action are retained at every coefficient prime.

source_statement: Finite polynomial families of integral primitives. \label{lem:ghost-primitive-family} Let \(T\) be a finite free \(\mathbb Z_\ell\)-module with a continuous \(G\)-action. Fix continuous rational two-cochains \(c_1,\ldots,c_m\in C^2(G,T\otimes\mathbb Q_\ell)\). Then \[ R=\left\{u\in\mathbb Z_\ell^m: \sum_i u_i c_i\in\delta C^1(G,T)\right\} \] is a closed finite free submodule of \(\mathbb Z_\ell^m\). There is a continuous \(\mathbb Z_\ell\)-linear map \(h:R\to C^1(G,T)\) satisfying \(\delta h(u)=\sum_i u_i c_i\). Each coordinate of \(h\), relative to finitely many fixed continuous cochains, is the restriction to \(R\) of a \(\mathbb Q_\ell\)-linear form on \(\mathbb Q_\ell^m\).
source_depends_on: C.1.3; noetherian closed submodules; finite polynomial family
audit_scope: Closedness and continuous choice of primitives for a finite polynomial parameter family are proved; no closedness of all global coboundaries is inferred.

source_statement: Compactness for a fixed abelian cocycle. \label{prop:ghost-compact-fibres} Every \(\mathscr S_{r,\ell}(a)\) is compact Hausdorff. More precisely, it is the continuous image of a closed subset \(X_r\subseteq\mathbb Z_\ell^{d_r}\), and its Hall coordinate functions are rational polynomials in these parameters, with continuous cochain coefficients.
audit_scope: Compactness is proved for one fixed literal abelian cocycle. It does not assert compactness of a varying family of ghosts.

source_statement: Exact compatibility equivalence for one fixed pair. \label{thm:ghost-fixed-pair-compatible} For any fixed power-completed Kummer pair \((A,B)\), the following two statements are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item For every integer \(r\geq1\), there exists a continuous section of \(E/\Gamma_{r+1}\Pi\to G_{\mathbb Q}\) whose abelian Kummer class is \((A,B)\). \item There exists a continuous section of \(E/\bigcap_r\Gamma_{r+1}\Pi\to G_{\mathbb Q}\) whose abelian Kummer class is \((A,B)\). \end{enumerate} The corresponding equivalence also holds with the requirement that all restrictions be geometrically conjugate to one fixed family of local point sections, or of local cuspidal sections, at every level.
source_depends_on: C.1.6; compact inverse-limit finite intersection argument
audit_scope: All integral classes for the same fixed pair are equivalent to one compatible full pronilpotent section, with the corresponding fixed local-matching variant.

source_statement: The weight-twelve, coefficient-691 kernel. \label{prop:ghost-h2-691} Put \(\ell=691\), \(T=\mathbb Z_{691}(12)\), and \(S=\{691,\infty\}\). Inflation is injective and its image has the following properties: \[ H^2_{\mathrm{cts}}(G_{\mathbb Q,S},T) \simeq\mathbb Z/691\mathbb Z \lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow H^2_{\mathrm{cts}}(G_{\mathbb Q},T). \] Every class in this image restricts to zero in \(H^2_{\mathrm{cts}}(G_{\mathbb Q_v},T)\) for every place \(v\). Its image in \(H^2(G_{\mathbb Q},T/691^nT)\) is zero for every \(n\geq1\).
source_depends_on: Integral Milnor sequence; Poitou–Tate duality; K22(Z) at 691; local duality
audit_scope: The nonzero weight-twelve coefficient-691 continuous class, its injective inflation, local vanishing and finite-coefficient vanishing are re-proved.

source_statement: An actual continuous extension with every finite reduction split. \label{cor:ghost-integral-extension} There is an exact sequence of profinite groups \[ 1\longrightarrow\mathbb Z_{691}(12) \longrightarrow\mathcal E\longrightarrow G_{\mathbb Q} \longrightarrow1 \] with no continuous group-theoretic section, such that its restriction to every \(G_{\mathbb Q_v}\) has a continuous section and \(\mathcal E/691^nT\to G_{\mathbb Q}\) has a continuous section for every \(n\geq1\).
source_depends_on: C.1.8; continuous two-cocycle extension construction
audit_scope: The actual profinite extension associated to the continuous two-cocycle has all stated splitting and nonsplitting properties; it is not identified with a curve quotient.

source_statement: The exact derived-limit kernel and a regular-prime example. \label{prop:ghost-uncountable-kernel} For every odd prime \(\ell\) and every \(r\geq2\), the kernel of the actual integral localization map is exactly \[ \ker\!\left(H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q},\mathbb Z_\ell(r)) \longrightarrow\prod_v H^2_{\rm cts} (G_{\mathbb Q_v},\mathbb Z_\ell(r))\right) \simeq\varprojlim_n^{\,1}H^1 (G_{\mathbb Q},\mathbb Z/\ell^n(r)). \] At \(\ell=3,r=2\), this kernel contains a subgroup isomorphic to \[ \frac{\prod_{j\geq1}\mathbb Z_3} {c_0(\mathbb Z_3)},\qquad c_0(\mathbb Z_3)= \{(z_j):z_j\longrightarrow0\text{ in }\mathbb Z_3\}. \] In particular it is uncountable. The unramified integral group \(H^2(G_{\mathbb Q,\{3,\infty\}},\mathbb Z_3(2))\) is nevertheless zero.
source_depends_on: Milnor exact sequence; finite-coefficient local-global injectivity; explicit residue tower
audit_scope: Exact odd-primary derived-limit localization kernel and the explicit product/c0 subgroup at weight two and coefficient three are proved.

source_statement: The ordinary continuous cup vanishes. \label{prop:ghost-ordinary-cup} Every ordinary completed pair \((A,B)\in\mathcal G_{\rm ord}\) satisfies \[ A\cup B=0\quad\hbox{in}\quad H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q},\widehat{\mathbb Z}(2)). \] This proves the continuous cup assertion used in SECTIONS A.27 without assuming its omitted strict localization comparison.
source_depends_on: Ordinary tame symbols; K2(Z); explicit local primitive; finite residue surjectivity; compact primitive fibres
audit_scope: Ordinary continuous cup vanishing is proved with compatible integral primitives, retaining the derived-limit issue and the two-primary real term.

source_statement: Every ordinary pair has an actual global class-two lift. \label{cor:ghost-class2-lift} Put \(U=\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}\), base it at the tangent vector \(\overrightarrow{01}\), and write \(\Pi=\pi_1(U_{\overline{\mathbb Q}},\overrightarrow{01})\). Every ordinary completed pair is the abelianization of a continuous section of \[ \pi_1(U,\overrightarrow{01})/\Gamma_3\Pi \longrightarrow G_{\mathbb Q}. \] Consequently no ordinary pair is excluded by unrestricted global lifting at nilpotency class one or two.
source_depends_on: C.1.11; explicit integral class-two section coordinates
audit_scope: The primitive produces a section in the actual arithmetic class-two quotient; no local central matching is claimed.

source_statement: Integral localization with the coefficient maps retained. \label{thm:ghost-strict-localization} For every prime \(\ell\) and every integer \(r\ge2\), put \(T=\mathbb Z_\ell(r)\), \(S=\{\ell,\infty\}\), and \[ R_\ell=\{(z_q)_{q\ne\ell}\in\prod_{q\ne\ell}\mathbb Z_\ell: z_q\longrightarrow0\},\qquad (d_rz)_q=(q^{r-1}-1)z_q. \] Fix compatible Tate coordinates at the finite residue fields. There is a natural, in those coordinates, exact sequence of abelian groups \[ 0\longrightarrow H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q,S},T) \xrightarrow{\rm inf}H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q},T) \xrightarrow{\Psi_{\ell,r}}R_\ell/d_rR_\ell \longrightarrow0. \] The quotient uses the actual image \(d_rR_\ell\). In particular this proves the exactness assertion used in SECTIONS A.65.8. For \(r=3\), inflation has zero source, so \(\Psi_{\ell,3}\) is an isomorphism for every \(\ell\), as asserted abstractly in SECTIONS A.46.2.
source_depends_on: Coefficient-compatible supports triangle; derived inverse limit; real-place H3 comparison; K4(Z)=0
audit_scope: Strict integral localization uses the literal image d_r R_ell, not its closure; degree-three fixed-ramification H2 is zero.

source_statement: Rational Magnus conjugacy detects pro-\(\ell\) conjugacy. \label{lem:ghost-magnus-conjugacy} Let \(F^{(\ell)}=\langle x,y\rangle^{(\ell)}\) be the free pro-\(\ell\) group, embedded by the Magnus map \(x\mapsto1+X\), \(y\mapsto1+Y\) in \(1+(X,Y)\mathbb Z_\ell\langle\!\langle X,Y\rangle\!\rangle\). The conjugacy relation induced on this group by the full unit group of \(\mathbb Q_\ell\langle\!\langle X,Y\rangle\!\rangle\) is exactly its own pro-\(\ell\) conjugacy relation.
source_depends_on: Integral cyclic-word sums; finite ell-group augmentation ideals; compact conjugator fibres
audit_scope: Rational formal conjugacy detects pro-ell conjugacy via integral cyclic words and compact conjugator fibres; rational series are not evaluated in finite group algebras.

Singleton local fibre at a boundary valuation. \label{prop:ghost-local-boundary} Let \(q
e\ell\) be primes and let \(t\in\mathbb Q_q\setminus\{0,1\}\) satisfy \((v_q(t),v_q(1-t))
e(0,0)\). In the geometrically pro-\(\ell\) arithmetic fundamental group of \(U_{\mathbb Q_q}\), the fibre of the abelianization map on geometric conjugacy classes of continuous sections over \[ (\kappa_\ell(t),\kappa_\ell(1-t)) \] consists of exactly the local point-section class of \(t\). Therefore every all-depth ordinary global pronilpotent section matches its prescribed ordinary local point at every coefficient prime \(\ell
e q\) and every finite place \(q\) of nonzero valuation support.
source_depends_on: C.1.16; Frobenius weights; rational Hall corrections; integral peripheral centralizer
audit_scope: The full local pro-ell section fibre is a singleton at a nonzero ordinary boundary valuation when ell differs from the rational place.

source_statement: Continuous first cohomology in weight two. \label{prop:ghost-h1-weight2} There are isomorphisms \[ H^1_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q},\mathbb Z_\ell(2)) \simeq \begin{cases} \mathbb Z/8,&\ell=2,\\ \mathbb Z/3,&\ell=3,\\ 0,&\ell\ge5, \end{cases} \qquad H^1_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q},\widehat{\mathbb Z}(2)) \simeq\mathbb Z/24. \] The latter group is generated by the integral continuous cocycle \(\eta(g)=(\chi(g)^2-1)/24\).
source_depends_on: Weibel IV.2.5, VI.4.3.1–2, VI.5.3; exact coefficient transition maps; tame K2 sequence
audit_scope: Integral weight-two H1 is Z/8 at two, Z/3 at three and zero otherwise, hence Z/24 with its stated generator.

source_statement: Exactly twenty-four class-two section classes. \label{cor:ghost-class2-fibre24} For every ordinary completed pair \((A,B)\), the fibre of geometric-conjugacy classes of continuous sections of the actual class-two arithmetic quotient above \((A,B)\) is a simply transitive \(\mathbb Z/24\)-set. For the geometrically pro-\(\ell\) quotient, the corresponding fibre has eight elements at two, three at three, and one at every \(\ell\ge5\). More explicitly, choose literal abelian cocycles \(a,b\) and one lift with central coordinate \(h\). Representatives for all twenty-four classes are \[ y^{b(g)}x^{a(g)}C^{h(g)+k\eta(g)}s_0(g), \qquad k\in\mathbb Z/24. \]
source_depends_on: C.1.12; C.1.18; vanishing of global weight-one invariants
audit_scope: Exactly twenty-four unrestricted class-two conjugacy classes are proved, with the missing stabilizer ruled out. They are not twenty-four locally matching classes.

source_statement: The exact coefficient-five class-two prefix. \label{lem:ghost-prefix-five} Choose a first pair \(q_0,r_0\) by the original A.44 rules, and put \[ a_1=3q_0^{24},\qquad b_1=-2r_0^{24},\qquad n_j=(j+4)!. \tag{45} \] Choose the old local roots \((\xi_p,\eta_p)\) in its stage \(j=1\), so that \(a_1\xi_p^{120}+b_1\eta_p^{120}=1\). Let \(P,R\) be positive rational integers that are units at \(q_0,r_0\), with \[ P\equiv\xi_p\pmod p,\qquad R\equiv\eta_p\pmod p \quad(p=q_0,r_0). \tag{46} \] There is a class-two homomorphism \[ \rho_*:G_{\mathbb Q}\longrightarrow H_5\rtimes\mathbb F_5^\times \tag{47} \] with abelian Kummer pair \((a_1,b_1)\), uniquely determined up to central geometric conjugacy by the two inertia prescriptions in the proof. It is unramified outside \(2,3,5,q_0,r_0\). Its image is the full group of order five hundred, and its fixed field \(L_*\) has maximal abelian subfield \(\mathbb Q(\mu_5)\). For every original A.44 continuation with the chosen stage-one local roots and with \[ q_j\equiv r_j\equiv1\pmod{q_0r_0} \quad(j\ge2), \tag{48} \] the coefficient-five reduction of every integral class-two section, after aligning its abelian cocycles, is centrally conjugate to \(\rho_*\). In particular this field is fixed before the choice of \(q_1\) and \(r_1\).
source_depends_on: C.1.11; C.1.15; C.1.18; original A.44 local invariant; exact integral primitive comparison; coefficient-five restricted-ramification cohomology
audit_scope: The first part of E.118 reconstructs the exact coefficient-five prefix, integral local primitives, unique finite central class, full order-500 image and maximal abelian subfield. That part does not use the later noncube restriction.

source_statement: A finite prefix determines every fixed class-two coefficient quotient. \label{lem:ghost-finite-prefix-determines} Fix \(\ell\ge5\) prime and \(N\ge1\). Let \(J_N\) be the least index with \(v_\ell((J_N+4)!)\ge N\). In an original A.44 prefix containing all indices \(i<J_N\), put \[ \begin{split} S_{\ell,N}&=\bigl(\{2,3\}\cup \{q_i,r_i:i<J_N\}\bigr)\setminus\{\ell\},\\ D&=N+\max_{p\in S_{\ell,N}}v_\ell(p-1). \end{split} \tag{76} \] Extend this prefix through an index \(L-1\), with \(L\ge J_N\) and \(v_\ell((L+4)!)\ge D\). Every integral class-two section of every ordinary original-A.44 continuation of that finite prefix has the same coefficient-\(\ell^N\) class-two reduction up to geometric conjugacy. After their abelian cocycles are aligned by the explicit representatives in the proof, the conjugacy is central.
source_depends_on: C.1.15; C.1.18; original factorial exponents; literal integral Kummer sums; exact tame relations and division by p−1 before reduction
audit_scope: The finite-prefix assertion for ell at least five is proved and extended to two and three with the needed Bockstein precision.

source_statement: The displayed fixed-depth outputs tend to the rational pair. \label{prop:ghost-a65-limit} The abelian pairs prescribed by the displayed congruence formulas in SECTIONS A.65 converge to \((3,-2)\) in the power-completion topology as the depth tends to infinity.
source_depends_on: Exact factorial exponents in supplied A.65 construction
audit_scope: The exact displayed historical A.65 sequence converges to (3,-2) for arbitrary N_R: R! divides the required C_R and both divided products are C_R-th powers. The ordinary locus is not closed, and fixed-pair compactness cannot be applied to the varying survivors.

source_statement: A factorial ordinary pair first excluded by local matching at class two. \label{thm:ghost-factorial-selmer32} There is a completely specified variant of the prime recursion of SECTIONS A.44, of the same form \[ A=3\prod_{j\ge0}q_j^{(j+4)!},\qquad B=-2\prod_{j\ge0}r_j^{(j+4)!}, \] whose first failure of everywhere locally point-or-cusp-matching nilpotent lifting is class two. The obstructing finite geometric quotient has order \(32\). This concerns local matching; it assigns no failure to unrestricted global class-two lifting.
source_depends_on: Explicit modified A.44 pair; genus-two cover; exact two-descent; finite residue check at 1129
audit_scope: The exact original-factorial variant with ordinary centre in 828+1129 Z_1129 is reconstructed. Its first everywhere locally point-or-cusp-matching failure is class two, detected by the actual order32 quotient; its unrestricted class-two fibre still has twenty-four classes.

source_statement: The displayed A.196 pair fails the ordinary local test. \label{prop:ghost-a196-scope} In \(k=\mathbb Q(\alpha)\), \(\alpha^3=3\), set \(A=649^8\alpha\), \(U=\alpha^2-2\), \(B=U^3\). Its image modulo ninth powers at the place above three belongs to no ordinary or cuspidal point image.

audit_scope: The exact 649^8 pair over Q(cuberoot(3)) is ordinary modulo cubes but neither ordinary nor cuspidal modulo ninth powers; the latter is the precise historical assertion.

source_statement: What the prime \(1129\) does to the third obstruction. \label{prop:ghost-1129-unramified} For the ordinary factorial witness of Theorem~\ref{thm:ghost-factorial-selmer32}, every global class-two section has zero local class-three obstruction at \(1129\), for every coefficient prime. At every coefficient prime \(\ell\ne1129\), its restriction there lifts to the entire geometrically pro-\(\ell\) local arithmetic fundamental group.
source_depends_on: C.1.15; valuation-zero Kummer coordinates at 1129; unramified pro-ell action; local duality
audit_scope: For the exact ordinary factorial 1129 witness every global class-two section has zero local third obstruction there at every coefficient prime. At each coefficient prime different from1129, its specified local class-two restriction lifts to the full geometrically pro-ell local extension.

source_statement: First unrestricted integral failure at class three. \label{thm:ghost-first-integral-class3} There is a recursively specified ordinary pair \[ A=3\prod_{j\ge0}q_j^{5(j+4)!},\qquad B=-2\prod_{j\ge0}r_j^{5(j+4)!}, \] with pairwise distinct primes \(q_j,r_j>3\), for which the first empty fibre of global continuous integral nilpotent sections is class three. Its class-two fibre has exactly twenty-four geometric-conjugacy classes. Every one has a nonzero local third obstruction at \(q_0\) in its coefficient-prime-five component. The reduction modulo \(25\) of that obstruction is already nonzero.

audit_scope: The exact scaled exponents 5(j+4)!, initial exponents 120 and 600, and first-prime q0 coefficient-five defect modulo25 are reconstructed. Every one of the twenty-four integral class-two classes is excluded.

source_statement: An A.44 prime choice first fails integrally at class three. \label{thm:ghost-original-first-integral-class3} There is a recursively specified choice of primes permitted by SECTIONS A.44, with its original exponents \(n_j=(j+4)!\), for which the ordinary pair \[ A=3\prod_jq_j^{n_j},\qquad B=-2\prod_jr_j^{n_j} \] has first unrestricted integral failure at nilpotency class three. Every integral class-two section above this pair has a nonzero local third obstruction at \(q_0\) in coefficient prime three, already detected modulo nine.
source_depends_on: C.2.5 cover argument; explicit H3 arithmetic descent; C.1.18; K2(Z) at three; A.44 original recursion
audit_scope: The selected original-factorial family has a coefficient-three class-three exclusion detected modulo nine, with the other central twists excluded at two.

source_statement: First class-three failure inside the compact-passing original family. \label{thm:ghost-passing-first-class3} There is a recursively specified original A.44 output \[ A=3\prod_{j\ge0}q_j^{(j+4)!},\qquad B=-2\prod_{j\ge0}r_j^{(j+4)!} \tag{55} \] for which every \(q_j\) has three a noncube and every \(r_j\) has two a noncube. It therefore passes every compact elliptic support-order test (16) and admits the full profinite affine-cover abelian section of Proposition~\ref{prop:ghost-all-passing-genjac}, with proper class zero. Nevertheless its first empty unrestricted integral nilpotent section fibre is class three. All twenty-four integral class-two section classes have a nonzero local third obstruction at \(q_1\), at coefficient prime five, already nonzero after reduction modulo twenty-five.
source_depends_on: C.1.20; C.3.5; C.3.10; exact Heisenberg/radical/cyclotomic fibre products; C.1.15 residue formula; original A.44 recursion
audit_scope: The exact compact-test-passing original family, coefficient-five defect at q1 modulo25, nonempty affine abelian cover fibre and empty class-three fibre are reconstructed.

source_statement: Dense class-three failure with the original factorial exponents. \label{thm:ghost-dense-class3} For every \(k\ge0\), the actual prefix maps satisfy \[ \begin{split} \operatorname{pr}_k(\mathscr F_3) &=\operatorname{pr}_k(\mathscr A),\\ \operatorname{pr}_k(\mathscr F_3\cap\mathscr A_c) &=\operatorname{pr}_k(\mathscr A_c). \end{split} \tag{64} \] Thus class-three-excluded outputs are dense among all original A.44 outputs, and among the outputs passing the compact tests. In the latter domain, every constructed pair has a full profinite section of the affine-cover abelian quotient with proper class zero, while its metabelian cover section fibre is empty. More precisely, after any specified finite prefix the construction chooses a coefficient prime \(\ell\ge5\) and a later support prime \(q_{\ell-4}\) at which every integral class-two section has nonzero third obstruction, already detected modulo \(\ell^2\). All exponents remain the original \((j+4)!\).

source_statement: Open dense failure and finite prefixes forcing exclusion. \label{cor:ghost-open-dense-class3} Let \(\mathscr U_3\subset\mathscr A\) consist of the original A.44 outputs having a nonzero local third-obstruction class at some coefficient prime \(\ell\ge5\), detected at some finite coefficient exponent. Then \(\mathscr U_3\) is open and dense in \(\mathscr A\), and \(\mathscr U_3\cap\mathscr A_c\) is open and dense in \(\mathscr A_c\). Every member has first unrestricted integral failure at class three. In particular, every finite legal prefix has a finite extension whose every ordinary legal continuation is excluded at class three. In the compact-passing domain such forcing prefixes can be chosen within that domain, retaining the affine abelian cover section and excluding its metabelian lifts.

source_statement: The exact coefficient-prime image. \label{lem:ghost-variable-exponent-image} Let \(d\ge2\), let \(24\mid C\), and let \(n=h!\), where \(h\ge2d^2\) and every prime divisor of \(C\) is at most \(h\). Put \[ E(Z)=Cn\prod_{r=2}^d(Z^r-1),\qquad D=Cd!n^d. \] For a prime \(p\mid n\), write \[ v=v_p(n),\quad e=v_p(d),\quad a_p=\begin{cases}1,&p\ne2,\\2,&p=2,\end{cases} \qquad W_p=v_p(C)+(d+1)v+v_p(d!)+a_p+e. \] The continuous map \[ F_p(z)=\exp\bigl(E(z)\log z\bigr) \] is a bijection from \(1+p^v+p^{v+a_p}\mathbb Z_p\) onto \[ F_p(1+p^v)\bigl(1+p^{W_p}\mathbb Z_p\bigr). \tag{VX.1} \] Every point of this domain satisfies \[ v_p(z-1)=v,\qquad v_p(E(z))=v_p(D), \qquad W_p\le2v_p(D). \tag{VX.2} \] The map preserves congruences modulo \(p^L\) between points of the domain. For positive integers in the domain it is the ordinary power \(z^{E(z)}\).

source_statement: Reconstruction of SECTIONS A.66. \label{thm:ghost-general-exponent-arithmetic} Fix \(d\ge2\), a positive integer \(C\) divisible by \(24\), and an integer \(J\ge2d^2\) at least every prime divisor of \(C\). Put \[ n_j=(j+J)!,\qquad D_j=Cd!n_j^d,\qquad E_j(Q)=Cn_j\prod_{r=2}^d(Q^r-1). \tag{VX.6} \] There are three sequences of distinct primes \(q_j,r_j,s_j>3\), disjoint from one another, for which \[ A=3\prod_{j\ge0}\frac{q_j^{E_j(q_j)}}{s_j^{E_j(s_j)}}, \qquad B=-2\prod_{j\ge0}\frac{r_j^{E_j(r_j)}}{s_j^{E_j(s_j)}} \tag{VX.7} \] are an ordinary completed unit-equation pair. Their valuations at two and three are respectively \((0,1)\), \((1,0)\), and their other nonzero valuation pairs are exactly \[ \begin{array}{c|c} q_j&(E_j(q_j),0)\\ r_j&(0,E_j(r_j))\\ s_j&(-E_j(s_j),-E_j(s_j)). \end{array} \tag{VX.8} \] Both coordinates have infinite support. In the global power completion, \(A/3\) and \(B/(-2)\) are \(C\)-th powers. The construction is a recursion by finite CRT conditions and specified Chebotarev classes; all its simultaneous field conditions are compatible.

source_statement: SECTIONS A.65, with its arithmetic and localization inputs proved. \label{thm:ghost-fixed-depth-survival} For every integer \(R\ge1\) and positive integer \(N\), there is an ordinary infinite-support completed pair \((A,B)\) and a continuous section \[ s:G_{\mathbb Q}\longrightarrow E_R=\pi_1(U,\overrightarrow{01})/\Gamma_{R+1}\Pi \] whose abelianization is \((A,B)\). Here all lower central subgroups are closed. The section agrees with the rational-point section of three in the actual finite arithmetic quotient defined by truncating the integral Magnus expansion at degree \(R\) and reducing its coefficients modulo \(N\), as specified in the proof. Its abelian pair is neither a rational point image nor a cuspidal image. The pair and the section in this statement are allowed to depend on \(R,N\).

source_statement: Selected fixed-depth ghosts have a finite later failure. \label{thm:ghost-unbounded-finite-failures} For every \(R\ge1\) and positive integer \(N\), the construction of Theorem~\ref{thm:ghost-fixed-depth-survival} can be made to give a pair \((A_{R,N},B_{R,N})\) whose first empty unrestricted integral nilpotent section fibre occurs at a finite class strictly larger than \(R\). It has no section of the full geometrically pro-five arithmetic fundamental group. The finite excluding class is asserted to exist; no formula for its least value is asserted. One fixed finite etale cover detects the full pro-five exclusion of all these selected examples: the point-three twist of the characteristic Heisenberg cover of geometric degree \(125\). The exact cover subgroup and the local comparison are specified below. The statement concerns these selected outputs of A.65, rather than every output of that construction.

source_statement: A weighted augmentation bound in the five-coordinate group. \label{lem:ghost-weighted-augmentation} Let \(p\ge5\) be a prime, let \(a\ge1\), and put \(M=p^a\). Let \(P_M\) be the free group of nilpotency class at most three and exponent dividing \(M\) on \(x,y\). It is a finite \(p\)-group of order \(M^5\). Write \[ c=[x,y],\qquad d=[c,x],\qquad e=[c,y], \qquad [u,v]=uvu^{-1}v^{-1}. \tag{FB.1} \] In the group algebra \(\mathbb F_p[P_M]\), its augmentation ideal \(I\) satisfies \[ I^{\,1+10(M-1)}=0. \tag{FB.2} \]

source_statement: An empty local fibre at an explicit integral class. \label{prop:ghost-finite-local-bound} Let \(p\ge5\), let \(q\ne p\) be a rational prime with \(q\equiv1\pmod p\), and let \(m\ne0\) be an integer. Put \(k=v_p(m)\) and \[ B(p,m)=10\bigl(p^{k+1}-1\bigr). \tag{FB.5} \] Use the tangential splitting at zero for \(U=\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}\). In the local geometrically pro-\(p\) arithmetic quotient of integral nilpotency class \(B(p,m)\), there is no continuous section with both of the following data: its tame inertia has abelian coordinates \((m,0)\); and its geometric Frobenius coordinate in the class-two exponent-\(p\) quotient \(H_p\) is a nonzero central element.

source_statement: A two-sided bound for the selected A.65 first failures. \label{cor:ghost-selected-failure-bound} For the selected pair of Theorem~\ref{thm:ghost-unbounded-finite-failures}, let \(q\) be its distinguished first positive support prime and \(m=E_0(q)\). Its first empty unrestricted integral nilpotent section fibre occurs at a class \(r\) satisfying \[ R<r\le10\bigl(5^{\,v_5(m)+1}-1\bigr). \tag{FB.11} \] In the parameters of Theorem~\ref{thm:ghost-general-exponent-arithmetic}, put \(d=\max(R,3)-1\), \(n=J!\), and \(a=v_5(n)\). The exact exponent is \[ v_5(m)=v_5(C)+da+v_5(d!). \tag{FB.12} \]

source_statement: Full reconstruction of SECTIONS A.72. \label{thm:ghost-finite-quotient-survival} Let \(N\) be an open subgroup of \(\Pi\), normal in \(E_U\), let \(Q=\Pi/N\), and fix the actual section \(s_3\) supplied by the rational point three. There are an integer \(N_0>0\), disjoint sequences of distinct primes \(q_j,r_j>3\), and an actual continuous section \[ \tau:G_{\mathbb Q}\longrightarrow E_U/(N\cap\overline{[\Pi,\Pi]}) =E_Q\mathbin{\times}_{E_{Q^{\rm ab}}}E_{\rm ab} \tag{FQ.1} \] with \(Q\)-component exactly \(s_3\) and abelian pair \[ A=3\prod_{j\ge0}q_j^{n_j},\qquad B=-2\prod_{j\ge0}r_j^{n_j},\qquad n_j=N_0(j+4)!. \tag{FQ.2} \] At every finite prime the pair is an ordinary unit-equation pair, and the entire local section in (FQ.1) is geometrically conjugate to the image of that ordinary point. At the real place it has the image of three. Both support sequences are infinite. The proof specifies the permissible parameters and the actual recursion, including all its local component maps.

source_statement: Selected A.72 pairs first fail at integral class three. \label{thm:ghost-a72-first-class3} Let \(N\triangleleft\Pi\) be open and normal in the full arithmetic group \(E_U\), and put \(Q=\Pi/N\). There is an ordinary infinite-support completed pair \((A,B)\) produced by the recursion of SECTIONS A.72, with a continuous section \[ \tau:G_{\mathbb Q}\longrightarrow E_U/(N\cap[\Pi,\Pi]) =E_Q\times_{E_{Q^{\rm ab}}}E_{\rm ab}, \tag{AQ.1} \] whose \(Q\)-component is the section of three and whose restriction at every finite place is geometrically conjugate to the image of its ordinary local point. At the real place it has the image of three. Nevertheless the unrestricted full integral nilpotent section fibre above \((A,B)\) is nonempty in class two and empty in class three. Consequently no one fixed finite geometric quotient, even retained jointly with the full abelianization and all the local conjugacies in (AQ.1), decides integral class-three liftability for ordinary completed pairs.

source_statement: The pointed Heisenberg cover as an open elliptic curve. \label{prop:ghost-elliptic-target} Let \(Y\to U\) be the degree-\(27\) finite etale cover defined by the class-two exponent-three geometric quotient \(H_3\) and the point-three section: its arithmetic fundamental group is the inverse image of that section in the arithmetic \(H_3\)-quotient. Its smooth compactification, pointed by the sheet above three, is \[ E':\ y^2=x^3+9. \] The open curve \(Y\) is the complement of the twenty-seven geometric points above \(0,1,\infty\). The map to \(U\) is the restriction of the explicit composite \[ E'\xrightarrow{\ \phi\ } E \xrightarrow{\ \iota^{-1}\ } C \xrightarrow{\ t=3u^3\ }\mathbb P^1, \quad E:y^2=x^3-243,\quad C:3u^3-2v^3=1, \tag{8} \] where \[ \phi(x,y)=\left(\frac{x^3+36}{x^2}, \frac{y(x^3-72)}{x^3}\right) \] and, for \(d=3u(u-1)-2v(v-1)\), \[ \iota(u,v)= \left(\frac{18(uv-1)}d, -\frac{27[3u(u+1)+2v(v+1)]}d\right). \tag{9} \] For every pair constructed in Theorem~\ref{thm:ghost-original-first-integral-class3}, its ordinary local point at \(q_0\) has no rational lift to \(Y\). There is no continuous section of the geometrically pro-three arithmetic fundamental group of \(Y\) whose pushforward to \(U\) has that abelian pair.

source_statement: The two exact three-isogeny Selmer calculations. \label{prop:ghost-elliptic-selmer} With the domain curve indicated by the isogeny, the Selmer groups are \[ \operatorname{Sel}^{\phi}(E'/\mathbb Q)=0, \qquad \operatorname{Sel}^{\psi}(E/\mathbb Q) =\langle6,12\rangle\simeq(\mathbb Z/3)^2 \] where the second group is a subgroup of \(\mathbb Q^\times/(\mathbb Q^\times)^3\). Both elliptic curves have trivial three-primary Tate--Shafarevich groups, and \[ \operatorname{rank} E'(\mathbb Q)=1, \qquad E'(\mathbb Q)^{\wedge3} =\mathbb Z_3 P_0\oplus(\mathbb Z/3)T. \] Here the completion is \(\varprojlim_n E'(\mathbb Q)/3^n\).

source_statement: Absolute continuous first cohomology of the target. \label{prop:ghost-elliptic-h1} The ordinary Kummer map is an isomorphism \[ E'(\mathbb Q)^{\wedge3} \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } H^1_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q},T_3E') =\mathbb Z_3\kappa(P_0) \oplus(\mathbb Z/3)\kappa(T). \] This is absolute Galois cohomology, with no imposed finite ramification set or local Selmer condition.

source_statement: A support-prime test for every original A.44 output. \label{prop:ghost-elliptic-support-test} The image of full geometrically pro-three sections of \(U\) whose abelian pairs are outputs of the original A.44 recursion is contained in the following explicit subset of those outputs: \[ \begin{split} &\operatorname{ord}_{E'(\mathbb F_{q_j})}((-2,1)) \text{ is prime to }3 \qquad\text{for every }q_j,\\ &\operatorname{ord}_{E'(\mathbb F_{r_j})}((3,-6)) \text{ is prime to }3 \qquad\text{for every }r_j. \end{split} \tag{16} \] Thus these tests apply to all choices of primes in A.44, not only the prescribed examples of Theorem~\ref{thm:ghost-original-first-integral-class3}.

This statement constructs the pairs and proves these tests; it does not assert a section above any of the pairs.

Consequently the compact local condition at two imposes no additional restriction on the coefficients \(a,b\) of \(a\kappa(P_0)+b\kappa(T)\).

source_statement: The exact generalized-Jacobian image. \label{prop:ghost-genjac-image} Let \(K=\pi_1(Y_{\overline{\mathbb Q}})\), viewed inside \(\pi_1(U_{\overline{\mathbb Q}})\) through the specified degree-twenty-seven cover. The quotient \(\pi_1(Y)/\overline{[K,K]}\) is the split arithmetic extension with kernel \(T\mathcal J\), split by \(O\); its inclusion into \(\pi_1(U)/\overline{[K,K]}\) retains the cover map. The image of its global continuous sections in the original completed unit coordinates contains \[ (3C^{27},-2D^{27}) \qquad(C,D\in\widehat{\mathbb Q^\times}). \tag{26} \] More precisely, at coefficient three its image consists exactly of the pairs \[ \begin{split} A&=3\left(u_0^a\frac{N_{K_0/\mathbb Q}\alpha_0} {N_{K_\infty/\mathbb Q}\alpha_\infty} \right)^3,\\ B&=-2\left(v_0^a\frac{N_{K_1/\mathbb Q}\alpha_1} {N_{K_\infty/\mathbb Q}\alpha_\infty} \right)^3, \\ &a\in\mathbb Z_3,\quad \alpha_i\in\widehat{K_i^\times}_3,\\ &u_0=\frac{253}{655},\quad v_0=-\frac{488}{655}. \end{split}\tag{27} \] All norms and powers in (27) are the continuous maps on the indicated multiplicative completions.

source_statement: Hasse norm principle for the three boundary fields. \label{prop:ghost-boundary-hasse-norm} Each algebra \(K_i\) of (25) is a field of degree nine. Its normal closure has group \(G=H_3\rtimes C_2\), of order fifty-four, with the involution acting by minus one on the two abelian Heisenberg generators and trivially on its centre. A point stabilizer is \(S_3\). Each \(K_i/\mathbb Q\) satisfies the Hasse norm principle: a rational number that is a norm at every completion is an actual global norm. Its norm-one torus also satisfies weak approximation.

source_statement: An unscaled A.44 family surviving the affine-cover abelian quotient. \label{prop:ghost-original-genjac-survival} The original recursion with exponents \((j+4)!\) admits ordinary infinite-support outputs with \[ q_j\equiv r_j\equiv1\pmod {27},\qquad 3\notin(\mathbb F_{q_j}^\times)^3, \quad2\notin(\mathbb F_{r_j}^\times)^3, \tag{39} \] and an actual global continuous section of \(\pi_1(U)/\overline{[K,K]}\) lying above that full completed pair. It factors through the generalized-Jacobian quotient of the pointed cover \(Y\), and its compact Tate-module class is zero at every coefficient prime.

Every output of the original A.44 recursion satisfying all the finite elliptic order tests (16) admits a full profinite section of \(\pi_1(U)/\overline{[K,K]}\), factoring through the generalized-Jacobian quotient of \(Y\) and having proper Tate-module class zero. In particular this conclusion holds for every original family constructed in Proposition~\ref{prop:ghost-elliptic-passing}; no additional congruence at three is needed.

The corresponding fibre for \[ \pi_1(Y)/\overline{[[K,K],[K,K]]} \tag{62} \] is empty. Thus every section in the former fibre has no lift through the displayed metabelian cover quotient.

source_statement: finite-coefficient vanishing for the actual ghost locus. Let $\mathcal G$ be the set of pairs $(A,B)\in \widehat{\Q^\times}^{\,2}$ such that, for each finite prime $p$, there is $x_p\in\Q_p\setminus\{0,1\}$ with $A_p=\kappa(x_p)$ and $B_p=\kappa(1-x_p)$. For every integer $n\geq1$ the image of $A\cup B$ in $H^2(G_\Q,\mu_n^{\otimes2})$ is zero. The continuous class lies in the kernel in the exact sequence \[ 0\longrightarrow\varprojlim_m^{\,1} H^1(G_\Q,\mu_{m!}^{\otimes2}) \longrightarrow H^2_{\rm cts}(G_\Q,\widehat{\Z}(2)) \longrightarrow\varprojlim_m H^2(G_\Q,\mu_{m!}^{\otimes2}) \longrightarrow0. \] Its restrictions to all continuous local cohomology groups, including the real one, are zero. No local section theorem is used.

source_statement: The rational unit-equation graph is closed and discrete. Give $\widehat{\Q^\times}$ the inverse-limit topology of A.10, and put \[ \mathcal R= \{(\kappa(t),\kappa(1-t)):t\in\Q\setminus\{0,1\}\} \subset\widehat{\Q^\times}^{\,2}. \] This subset is closed and discrete. Every Cauchy net in $\mathcal R$ is eventually constant. For a pair $(A,B)\notin\mathcal R$, there is a positive integer $N$ such that no rational $t\ne0,1$ has both $[t]_N=A_N$ and $[1-t]_N=B_N$ in $\Q^\times/(\Q^\times)^N$.

source_statement: Infinitely supported ordinary-local solutions of the completed unit equation. There are recursively specified pairwise distinct primes $q_j,r_j>3$, for $j\ge0$, such that, with $n_j=(j+4)!$, the completed products \[ A=3\prod_{j\ge0}q_j^{n_j}, \qquad B=-2\prod_{j\ge0}r_j^{n_j} \quad\text{in }\widehat{\Q^\times} \tag{A.44.1} \] have the following properties. At every finite prime $p$ their localizations are the Kummer classes of ordinary nonzero numbers $x_p,y_p\in\Z_p$ with $x_p+y_p=1$. Thus $(A,B)\in\mathcal G$. Their valuation vectors are \[ \begin{array}{c|cc} p&v_p(A)&v_p(B)\\\hline 3&1&0\\ 2&0&1\\ q_j&n_j&0\\ r_j&0&n_j\\ \text{all other primes}&0&0. \end{array} \tag{A.44.2} \] Both coordinates have infinite support, so neither is the Kummer class of a rational number. The construction uses no local section theorem.
source_depends_on: A.10; exact radical-field commutators; Chebotarev; Hensel; Jacobi sums
audit_scope: The original exact exponents (j+4)!, local ordinary limits, all valuation coordinates and recursive prime choices are re-proved.

source_statement: No fixed finite puncture set forces rationality. Choose $J\ge6$ at least as large as every prime divisor of $C$, and put \[ n_j=(j+J)!,\quad D_j=6Cn_j^3,\quad E_j(Q)=Cn_j(Q^2-1)(Q^3-1). \tag{A.62.1} \] There are distinct primes $q_j,r_j,s_j>3$ for which \[ A=3\prod_{j\ge0}\frac{q_j^{E_j(q_j)}}{s_j^{E_j(s_j)}}, \qquad B=-2\prod_{j\ge0}\frac{r_j^{E_j(r_j)}}{s_j^{E_j(s_j)}}. \tag{A.62.2} \] Every finite localization is the Kummer pair of an ordinary $x_p\in\Q_p\setminus\{0,1\}$. At two and three its valuation pairs are $(0,1)$ and $(1,0)$; at $q_j,r_j,s_j$ they are $(E_j(q_j),0)$, $(0,E_j(r_j))$, and $(-E_j(s_j),-E_j(s_j))$, respectively. Thus this construction supplies both factors $Q^2-1$ and $Q^3-1$ with a factorial factor tending to zero in $\widehat\Z$. The class-four construction uses $C=24$ and $J=6$.
